stem: One line of this quality plan is not a usable quality requirement. Click the metric that cannot be checked.
explanation: 'Good atmosphere' has no measurable metric and no target, so nobody can say afterwards whether it was met. Quality planning answers four questions: what standard, what metric, what target, and how will we check. A requirement that fails any of them is a wish, not a quality requirement.

stem: One entry in this risk register is not a risk at all. Click the row that belongs somewhere else.
choices: R1 — the supplier may deliver the panels late
R2 — the lead developer has resigned this morning
R3 — the new tax rules may change before launch
R4 — the integration may fail load testing
explanation: R2 has already happened, so it is an issue, not a risk: a risk is an uncertain future event, while an issue is a problem affecting the project now. It needs an issue log and an immediate response, not a probability and an impact score. A risk becomes an issue the moment it occurs.
